Subject: Re: Inventory & attestation for no-train / prompt ownership request

Thanks — I worked with infra to pull a concise inventory and attached a one‑page playbook (redwood-provenance-playbook.pdf) that explains the difference between:

- Ephemeral request-level KV cache (per-node, short TTL) — used for latency, never persisted across model checkpoints.
- API request logs (retained for troubleshooting/abuse) — default 30 days, configurable per-tenant when on Dedicated/Private.
- Telemetry and aggregate metrics — anonymized, no raw prompts retained after 90 days unless customer opt-in for analytics.

For ClearHealth (since you're on Hosted API): default retention for API logs is 30 days and we can commit in contract to reduce to 0 days on request for data subject content (we retain structured telemetry). The playbook includes a draft attestation snippet you can copy into Schedule A.

Attestation snippet (draft):
"Redwood will not use Customer prompts, responses, or other Customer Content to train or improve its models for general-purpose model updates without Customer's prior written opt‑in. Redwood may process Customer Content for providing the Service, for security and abuse prevention, and for system reliability, subject to the retention limits described in Schedule A."

I also attached the dataflow inventory xlsx with the column "cross-border" populated for subprocessors we use in EU/asia regions.

—Jonas
